title: Lou Singer and 'If I Had a Ribbon Bow'
summary: She explains the song by Lou Singer, which became popular, and why they recorded it.

blocks.x: -- on tape, and I was asking Maxine Sullivan about the August 22, 1939 session in which Alec Wilder was involved.

Yeah. I think I mentioned the fact that, by this time Claude and I were no longer working together. And I had to sort of look around and find somebody of the same caliber to help me with selection of material, and also making the arrangements. Lou Singer, who happened to be working at Leeds (Music), you know, doing the transcriptions -- he had also made arrangements for John Kirby Orchestra. So we had a relationship there. He dug up some material and got together for this date, and Alec Wilder made the arrangements. As you know, 'Jackie Boy' and 'Turtle Dove' are more in keeping, you know, with the tradition style.
Yeah. Didn't he also write, 'If I had A Ribbon Bow'?

Yes, Lou Singer wrote 'If I Had A Ribbon Bow'. That became a very popular thing, because it was sort of unusual. And, of course, 'Sing Something Simple', 'It's A Very Old Ditty', and 'Ill Wind' was from the 1934 rendition of the Cotton Club Show. I believed -- I guess I recall that Adelaide Hall had introduced it in that show. She did the 'Ill Wind.' This was supposed to replace the previous editions -- 'Stormy Weather', which Ethel Waters did.

But I remembered it and I always did like the tune. So we decided to record 'Ill Wind.' I think the -- you'll notice that the instrumentation and the arrangments is almost the same -- same sort of a combination of instruments that we used on the earlier records, because that particular instrumentation became identified with my selections too.
